facts.fact: A law article says that births, deaths and marriages are registered on declaration in paper registers kept in three copies at the civil status registration centres in the councils, with a counterfoil at the Court of First Instance, and that civil records are 'only' kept on hard copies up to the present; it argues this from the wording of the 1981 ordinance as amended in 2011 and gives no date, so the date is the publication date.

The same article states that Cameroon has not adopted digital records management for civil records and attributes no identification number at birth, and recommends an electronic system; it does not mention the 2024 civil registration law or any pilot; date is the publication date.

systems.country_label: civil status registration registers; counterfoil registers
systems.owner: civil status registration centres in the councils; duplicates at Courts of First Instance
systems.tiers: all centres, per the article; special registries under sub-divisional officers; diplomatic missions for events abroad

note: A doctrinal article reasoning from the 1981 ordinance; it does not report a survey of offices.
